doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Peter Gunn, Pink Panther and Henry Mancini
summary: He knew Mancini from Universal and played on Peter Gunn; Mancini matched players to tunes, and the orchestra applauded the Pink Panther take.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Well you happened to play on a couple of things where you could be one of the most heard saxophonists around — tell us about how Henry Mancini started to use you.

I had worked at Universal and had played on — Henry Mancini was kind of a junior writer out there at that time. So I played on several things with him before that. I’d also played on his “Peter Gunn.” And I had recorded “Peter Gunn” — I can’t think of the trumpet player’s name — but I’d recorded “Peter Gunn” on another record and it turned out to be a million seller. And this was —
I didn’t know that was you on “Peter Gunn.”

This was instead of Henry Mancini’s recording. I’ll think of the trumpet player’s name in a minute. So we had crossed paths before. And Henry had the talent of matching the player with the tune you know. He would call just the right saxophone player for what he was writing on. Just the right harmonica player, or, you know, he knew players quite well and he knew music. He had a knack for putting stuff together that matched, and I guess that’s how I came to work on his “Pink Panther.”
It’s a classic I think you could say. Certainly had a sound to it. Did you have any idea at the time that it was going to become such a — one of those tunes that everybody can whistle.

No. Of course not. But we did have an idea at the time that it was a great piece of music because it was like eight o’clock on a cold winter morning and I forget how many, it was a full orchestra with strings and everything, and after the tune was recorded, after the performance of the tune the orchestra applauded.
They liked it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
